title: Brakes, steering or gas pedal problem while driving
h1: Brakes, steering or gas pedal acting up
metaDesc: Brake pedal hard or sinking to the floor, gas pedal stuck, or steering suddenly heavy? What to do right now to slow down and stop safely.
first: Brake pedal suddenly very hard: push it with steady, heavy force and keep pushing. Don't pump it.
Brake pedal sinks to the floor: pump it hard and fast, even if you have ABS. Shift to a lower gear and put the parking brake on slowly.
Gas pedal stuck or car speeding up on its own: press the brake firmly and hold it (don't pump), and shift to neutral.
Steering suddenly heavy: grip the wheel with both hands, slow down gently and pull over when it's safe.
Turn on your hazard lights and steer to a safe spot. Once stopped, don't drive it again. Have it towed.
dont: Don't turn the engine off while you're moving unless nothing else works, and never turn the key to LOCK: you can lose steering.
Don't pump a brake pedal that's hard. That uses up the little power boost that's left.
Don't yank the parking brake on all at once. If the back of the car starts to slide, ease it off a little.
Once stopped, don't drive it again until it's checked.

steps.h: Brake pedal is suddenly very hard
steps.t: The brake booster has lost power, so the car needs much more force to stop and will take longer. Push the pedal with steady, heavy force and keep pushing. Don't pump it. Steer to a safe spot and stop.

steps.h: Brake pedal sinks to the floor
steps.t: Pump the pedal hard and fast. This can build up enough pressure to slow you, even if your car has ABS. After 3 or 4 pumps you'll know if it's helping. Shift to a lower gear so the engine helps slow you. Put the parking brake on slowly. If the back of the car starts to slide, ease the parking brake off a little.

steps.h: Gas pedal stuck or car speeds up on its own
steps.t: Press the brake firmly and hold it. Don't pump. Shift to neutral and steer to a safe spot. Once stopped, turn the engine off. With a push-button start you may need to hold the button for a few seconds. Check that a floor mat isn't trapping the pedal.
If the power steering stops working, you can still steer, but it takes much more effort. Grip the wheel with both hands, slow down gently, and pull over when it's safe.
Ease off the gas, brake gently, turn on your hazard lights and steer to a safe stop if you can.

call: Call 911 if you can't get the car stopped safely or off the road, or anyone is hurt.
Once you're stopped, call roadside help for a tow.
